builder_plan.scenario: An agent looks good in demos, but you cannot tell which product tasks it fails.
builder_plan.change: Use the study's evaluation idea to inspect a small set of tasks with human-checked answers.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current evaluator and a manually reviewed reference set.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Agreement with human review, missed failures, false alarms, and evaluation cost per task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: $μ$-Bench: Benchmarking Multi-User Task Completion in Shared Interaction Voice Agents
summary: μ-Bench replaces ad hoc single-user or scripted voice-agent evaluation with closed-loop, full-duplex multi-user simulation scored by session-level Joint Task Success and ATC failure diagnostics. Adoption costs the engineering effort of running 800 simulated multi-user scenarios against candidate systems, plus API or inference spend, without yielding any model improvement by itself. It can fail to predict production behavior if the reader's deployment differs in domain, acoustics, or group size, and its results indicate open-weight models below 20% success are unsuitable for multi-user voice deployments regardless of evaluation effort.
rationale: The paper is an evaluation benchmark, not a deployable method, but it is directly relevant if the team ships or selects shared-space multi-user voice agents, since it shows current open-weight options are not production-ready for this setting.
technique: Multi-user voice agent benchmark with joint task success

claims.statement: μ-Bench replaces ad hoc single-user or scripted voice-agent evaluation with closed-loop, full-duplex multi-user simulation scored by session-level Joint Task Success and ATC failure diagnostics. Adoption costs the engineering effort of running 800 simulated multi-user scenarios against candidate systems, plus API or inference spend, without yielding any model improvement by itself. It can fail to predict production behavior if the reader's deployment differs in domain, acoustics, or group size, and its results indicate open-weight models below 20% success are unsuitable for multi-user voice deployments regardless of evaluation effort.
Proprietary voice agents peak at 62.24% tool-free and 65.44% tool-augmented Joint Task Success; open-weight models remain below 20%, with attribution and threading the main failure loci.
